Class TypeRef<T>

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.codec.spi.TypeRef<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the captured type
public abstract class TypeRef<T> extends Object
Super type token capturing a full generic type at compile time, surviving erasure.

Instantiate as an anonymous subclass to capture a parameterized type: 

TypeRef<List<Person>> ref = new TypeRef<>() {};

A parameterized type can also be built at run time from the type references of its arguments, which keeps the compiler in the loop even when the argument is only known to the caller: 

TypeRef<List<O>> batch = TypeRef.listOf(elementType);   // TypeRef<O> supplied at run time

Equality and hashing are based on the captured Type, so instances are safe to use as cache keys; a type built with listOf(TypeRef) and the same type captured by an anonymous subclass are equal.

    • parameterized

      public static <T> TypeRef<T> parameterized(Class<? super T> raw, TypeRef<?>... arguments)
      A reference to any generic class applied to the given type arguments — your own Envelope<O> built from a TypeRef<O>, for example. The typed combinators (listOf(TypeRef), mapOf(TypeRef, TypeRef) and friends) cover the JDK collections; this covers every other generic class. T is taken from the assignment context, so declare the reference you mean: 
      TypeRef<Envelope<O>> ref = TypeRef.parameterized(Envelope.class, elementType);

      The class literal is a witness for T: because a raw type is a supertype of each of its parameterizations, Class<? super T> lets the compiler reject TypeRef<List<O>> ref = parameterized(Set.class, o) and TypeRef<Object> alike. The arity of arguments is checked at construction, and a class with no type parameters is rejected. What remains unchecked is the identity and order of arguments against T's own type arguments, and T naming a subtype of raw ( TypeRef<LinkedList<O>> from List.class). Such a mismatch does not fail in the codec: decode succeeds with a value of the built type, and the caller sees a ClassCastException where the decoded value is first used. Round-trip a reference built here once in a test.

      Type Parameters:
      T - raw applied to arguments
      Parameters:
      raw - the generic class, such as Envelope.class
      arguments - one type reference per type parameter of raw, in declaration order; each must be a reference type, not a primitive
      Returns:
      a reference to raw applied to arguments
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if raw, arguments or any argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if raw declares no type parameters, if the number of arguments does not match the number it declares, or if an argument is a primitive type

    • rawClass

      public Class<T> rawClass()
      Returns the erased class of the captured type: List.class for List<String>, the class itself for a non-generic type.

      This method contains the one unchecked cast in the codebase. It is sound by construction: a TypeRef<T> captures T and nothing else, so the erasure of the captured type is the erasure of T. Backends use the result with Class.cast(Object) — a checked cast — instead of an unchecked (T) cast of their own; every other cast in the reactor is a checked Class.cast or none at all, and no new unchecked cast is permitted anywhere else. The build compiles with -Xlint:all,-processing,-unchecked -Werror: the unchecked category is off precisely and only because of this method, since Java cannot express the type-token bridge without it and cannot write an unchecked cast without a warning.

      Returns:
      the erased class of T
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the captured type has no single erased class (a wildcard or a generic array type)
